name: Sodium smart-account session-key validation bypass draining Lumi Finance users
summary: Sodium._validateSignature authorizes the ERC-4337 executeWithSodiumAuthSession path whenever the session-key address read out of the userOp's own callData (bytes 16..36) equals the signer address read out of the userOp's own signature blob, and never checks that address against the wallet's stored session records the way the execute branch does through isSessionOwner. checkValidSodiumSignature type 0x01 takes the signer from the signature itself and resolves it through SignatureChecker, so an attacker-deployed ERC-1271 contract that returns the magic value for any digest makes signer, session key and validation all attacker-controlled. validateUserOp then unconditionally runs _payPrefund, moving the victim wallet's ETH to the EntryPoint where the attacker is the bundler beneficiary, and _approvePaymasterToken, which asks the userOp-supplied paymaster for getTokenAllowanceCast and grants exactly the allowance the attacker's own paymaster requests. The attacker set callGasLimit to 0 so every execution phase reverted out of gas while the validation-phase prefunds and ERC20 approvals persisted, then drained the approved balances with transferFrom.
notes: The Sodium wallet proxy resolves its implementation with ADDRESS SLOAD, so the pointer lives in the wallet's own storage slot keyed by its address. That slot is 0x0 at block 225855008 and 0x000000000000000000000000b5bc46df04dee31d219e7664122e29eed9506b8b from the wallet's creation block 225855009 through the pre-exploit block 483353616, and the proxy runtime hash is unchanged over the same interval, so the defect-bearing implementation became active for this execution context at its creation and stayed active.

Quantities are the exact depletion of the victim Sodium smart accounts, reconstructed from every ERC20 Transfer whose sender carries the Sodium proxy runtime and whose recipient is one of the seven attacker addresses (3383 wallets, 5790 transfers, blocks 483390113-483407358) plus the sum of EntryPoint UserOperationEvent actualGasCost across the attacker's 113 defect-executing transactions (5449 wallets, 8657 user operations, 0.152366822290852271 ETH). Inbound WETH and stablecoins from the three Uniswap V3 pools are the attacker's own swap proceeds and are excluded so nothing is double counted. LUAUSD is valued at realised proceeds: the attacker sold the entire stolen 74480.723661281941687839 LUAUSD into Curve in two transactions for 48399.605758 USDT0, an effective 0.6493678878437041 per unit, because his own selling moved LUAUSD from 0.965 to 0.547 within the hour. The stolen 65964.433640948840615208 LUA is left unvalued: DefiLlama returns an unchanged 3.1248490646990934 quote for every timestamp around the incident and no quote at all afterwards, so that figure is a stale mark rather than a price at which this block could have been sold, and the attacker never realised more than 16000 LUA onchain. The recorded USD total is therefore a floor; published reporting of about 264000 USD marks the LUA leg at that stale quote.
The stolen 65964.433640948840615208 LUA is carried without a USD value because no realisable price for that quantity exists, so loss.usd.amount is a floor rather than the full depletion.

A second, unverified Sodium implementation 0x46516e846ccba95fefc8da6a3cbab875367e5c46 was exploited through the same failure in the same campaign and is not represented as a separate target; curve deduplication by (incidentId, failureModeId) would collapse it into this observation in any case.
